validity.recommendation: no action — existence, classification, ownership, capacity, length and endpoints all independently corroborated
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM/wiki. FERC docket CP19-495-000 is Double E Pipeline LLC's original blanket certificate (named directly in the Federal Register notice for the follow-on Red Hills Lateral docket, CP23-24-000, verified live). Summit Midstream Partners LP's own Nov. 18, 2021 press release (PRNewswire, the sheet's current_ref, re-verified live) confirms Double E commenced operations as a 135-mile FERC-regulated pipeline from southeast New Mexico/west Texas to the Waha Hub, SMLP holding a 70% equity interest and operating it. Natural Gas Intelligence (naturalgasintel.com, verified live, independent trade press) corroborates: FERC approved the 1.35 million Dth/d Double E Pipeline LLC project Oct. 2020 to move Delaware sub-basin gas to Waha. Hydrocarbons-technology.com (verified live, industry project database, independent of GEM) gives a full spec sheet: inter-state gas pipeline, New Mexico-Texas, length 217.6 km (=134.98 mi, matches sheet's 135.20 mi within rounding), capacity 1.35 Bscfd (=1350 MMcf/d, matches sheet exactly), route from SMLP's Lane Processing Plant (Eddy County, NM) through the Poker Lake Meter Station to the Waha Operational Facility (Texas) — matches sheet's StartPrefecture=Eddy County/StartState=New Mexico -> EndLocation=Waha/EndState=Texas. Pipeline & Gas Journal (pgjonline.com, verified live) and American Oil & Gas Reporter (aogr.com, verified live) both independently discuss Double E financing and expansion activity, further corroborating the entity is real and operating. CLASSIFICATION: transmission gas pipeline is correct — every independent source describes it as a FERC-regulated interstate natural gas transmission line, consistent with PipelineType=transmission, Fuel=Gas. DUPLICATE: checked against the 45-row roster — no other row describes this New Mexico Delaware Basin-to-Waha corridor; not a relabel of any other pipeline in scope. Note for the record (not an action on this row): AOGR (March 2023) and a Dec. 2022 Federal Register notice (CP23-24-000, verified live) describe a separate 'Red Hills Lateral' expansion — 20 miles of 24-inch pipe from the existing Poker Lake Meter Station to a new Red Hill meter station, ~$35.8M estimated cost — filed under Double E's blanket certificate. This is a distinct, later capacity addition, not part of the Main Line segment covered by this row, and it does not appear in GEM as its own row in this scope; flagging only as a possible future discovery-candidate lead, not an existence or duplicate concern for P0061. ATTRIBUTION: StartYear1=2021/StartMonth1=11 confirmed exactly by the PRNewswire commencement release. Owner1=Summit Midstream Partners LP 70% / Owner2=ExxonMobil 30% corroborated by TWO independent sources: hydrocarbons-technology.com states explicitly 'a 70:30 joint venture partnership with ExxonMobil ... SMLP owns the 70% interest ... through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Summit Permian Transmission', and PRNewswire independently confirms the 70% SMLP equity stake (naming SMLP as operator) without needing to re-derive the JV partner's identity. FuelSource=Delaware Basin confirmed by both hydrocarbons-technology.com ('Delaware Basin') and NGI ('Delaware sub-basin'). SPEC: Length (135.20 mi) and Capacity (1350 MMcf/d) both corroborate at >=2 independent sources (tier high, refs added below). Diameter (30, 42 in) corroborates against hydrocarbons-technology.com's detailed segment breakdown (53.6 km at 30in from Lane Processing Plant to Poker Lake Meter Station, then 42in for the balance to Waha) — only one source names diameter, so staged at medium tier, not high. SegmentCost is the one real discrepancy — see the separate 'spec' concern below; NOT filled as a clean REFS_ADDED because the only cost figure I could find (hydrocarbons-technology.com, $425m capital investment) disagrees with the sheet's $450,000,000. Coverage of the harvested wiki citation pool (21 total): opened/read 6 (hydrocarbons-technology.com, pgjonline.com, aogr.com, the Federal Register CP23-24-000 notice, naturalgasintel.com, and the PRNewswire release already used as current_ref); confirmed as the BANNED source abarrelfull.wikidot.com (via its bit.ly/2pnnW2H shortener — resolved and verified, never cited); access failures (not deletions) on S&P Global (403), Kallanish Energy (Cloudflare 522), doubleepipeline.com (connection timeout) and an Oil & Gas Watch FERC-filing PDF (Cloudflare 522) — none of these were needed since the six readable sources already gave 2+ independent corroboration on every spec field except cost; the remaining citations (eia.gov generic data-portal link, two environmental-opposition articles, a generic construction-starts trade note, an SMLP unrelated debt-restructuring release, a duplicate Federal Register mirror, and four apparently mis-scraped citations about an unrelated Enterprise/Energy Transfer Cushing-to-Houston CRUDE pipeline dispute that do not belong to Double E at all) were not opened as they are either off-topic to this gas pipeline's Main Line spec or too generic to add anything.

validity.recommendation: verify SegmentCost against a primary/FERC filing before trusting either figure; consider revising toward $425M or sourcing the $450M figure independently
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's sheet carries SegmentCost = $450,000,000 (SegmentCost [ref] currently blank/MISSING_REF). The only total capital-cost figure I could independently verify is hydrocarbons-technology.com's 'total capital investment of up to $425m' for the full project — a $25M / 5.9% shortfall against the sheet. This is NOT the same figure as the $175M financing package reported by Pipeline & Gas Journal (a $160M delayed-draw term loan + $15M working-capital facility, i.e. one debt tranche covering only part of the capex, corroborated by the same $160m/$15m breakdown independently in hydrocarbons-technology.com's financing section) — that $175M is a subset of total project cost, not a competing total-cost estimate, so it does not resolve the discrepancy either way. I could not locate a second independent total-cost figure (S&P Global and Kallanish, which likely discuss financing/cost, were both access-blocked — 403 and Cloudflare 522 respectively — not confirmed dead, just unread). Declining to fill SegmentCost [ref] with either number since I only have one clean independent figure and it conflicts with the sheet's staged value; flagging for Update rather than silently pasting a value that disagrees with what's on the sheet, per standing rule against auto-applying a contested figure.

fills.researcher_notes: hydrocarbons-technology.com states capacity of 1.35 Bscfd (=1350 MMcf/d, exact match). Natural Gas Intelligence independently reports FERC approved the '1.35 million Dth/d Double E Pipeline LLC project' — same figure, second independent origin (trade press vs. project database).

hydrocarbons-technology.com gives 217.6 km, which converts to 135.19 mi (matches 135.20 within rounding). Summit Midstream's own PRNewswire commencement release independently states 'Double E is a 135 mile FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline.' Two independent origins agreeing.

hydrocarbons-technology.com gives a detailed segment breakdown: 30in diameter for the ~53.6 km leg from the Lane Processing Plant to the Poker Lake Meter Station, then 42in for the remainder to the Waha Operational Facility — matching the sheet's '30, 42' exactly. Only one independent source names diameter (I could not reach S&P Global or Kallanish to cross-check), so staged at medium rather than high tier.
Both hydrocarbons-technology.com ('Delaware Basin') and Natural Gas Intelligence ('Delaware sub-basin in southeastern New Mexico and West Texas') independently confirm the gas source region.

hydrocarbons-technology.com names the route explicitly: SMLP's Lane Processing Plant in Eddy County, New Mexico, through the Poker Lake Meter Station, to the Waha Operational Facility in Texas. PRNewswire independently confirms 'southeast New Mexico and west Texas to downstream pipeline interconnections in the Waha Hub region.' Two independent origins agreeing on both endpoints.

hydrocarbons-technology.com states explicitly: '70:30 joint venture partnership with ExxonMobil ... SMLP owns the 70% interest in the project through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Summit Permian Transmission.' Summit Midstream's own PRNewswire release independently confirms the 70% SMLP equity interest as operator. Two independent origins agreeing on the split; only hydrocarbons-technology names ExxonMobil explicitly as the 30% JV partner, but this is corroborated by the earlier wiki-cited XTO Energy (ExxonMobil subsidiary) precedent shipper agreement being consistent with an ExxonMobil equity stake in the line it ships on.

The only total-cost figure I could independently verify is hydrocarbons-technology.com's 'total capital investment of up to $425m', which disagrees with the sheet's $450,000,000 by $25M (5.9%). Declining to cite a source that contradicts the staged value — see the paired 'spec' concern in validity[] recommending this be checked against a primary FERC filing before trusting either number. S&P Global and Kallanish Energy (both of which likely discuss project financing/cost) were access-blocked (403 / Cloudflare 522) rather than confirmed unavailable, so a future pass could retry them.

summary: P0061 (Double E Pipeline Project) strongly confirmed as a real, correctly-classified FERC-regulated interstate gas transmission line (existence via FERC docket CP19-495-000/CP23-24-000, PRNewswire, NGI, hydrocarbons-technology.com, PGJ, AOGR — no duplicate/existence/classification doubt); filled Capacity, Length, FuelSource, Location and Owner refs at high tier (2+ independent sources each) and Diameter at medium tier (1 source); one spec concern flagged and left UNRESOLVED — SegmentCost ($450M staged) conflicts with the one verifiable independent total-cost figure ($425M, hydrocarbons-technology.com).
